card.title: Short Story 6 — Two Little Soldiers (Guy de Maupassant)

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The story at a glance "Two Little Soldiers" by Guy de Maupassant is a small story with a fatal centre: two Breton conscripts, Luc Le Ganidec and Jean Kerbalan, poor friends from the same village, serving far from home. Their one pleasure is Sunday walks by the river — until they begin, secretly, to watch a young milkmaid who lives at a farmhouse.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Two orphans find family feeling in each other — irony when a woman divides them.
Maupassant's twist ending: the 'third little soldier' is the baby; explain the irony.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Trick 3: The ending's irony: the woman was married all along — the soldiers' rivalry was pointless; name this dramatic irony explicitly.  ·  ## The characters worth an essay **Jean Kerbalan** is the story's centre of gravity: quiet, loyal, and in love without knowing it until the knowledge is fatal. Watch what Maupassant gives him — almost no dialogue. His love is conducted entirely in silences: the extra coin he does not spend, the sadness he cannot name, the final Sunday alone. The sketch the exam wants is a study in the unsaid.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## The themes worth an essay **Friendship and betrayal** — the central theme: not a dramatic treachery but an omission, which is why it kills; the friend who shares everything except the one thing that matters. **Loneliness of the displaced** — the soldiers' homesickness is the story's soil: the girl matters because she is a piece of the countryside they lost.…  ·  ## How NEB asks it **"Why were the two soldiers sad on Sundays?" (4 marks)** — homesickness first, then Jean's unnamed love; separate the two sadnesses and the answer is complete. **"How did Luc betray Jean?"** — the concealment, not the courtship: he used their shared walks as cover and told him nothing.…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. Why do the two soldiers visit the countryside? (1 mark) — to escape barracks loneliness and enjoy the company of the kind countrywoman.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The plot, retold with an eye on its turns The setup is friendship in uniform: two soldiers of the same countryside, "little" in the title because they are small in the army's world — underpaid, homesick, joined at the hip on Sundays. The routine: coffee at the inn, the walk along the river, the recollection of home.…  ·  ## The devices, with evidence - **Foreshadowing** — the master device: Jean's growing sadness, his silence, his lost appetite — Maupassant marks the tragedy in advance and lets the reader walk into it unprepared anyway. - **Irony** — the story's bitterest resource: the secret courted under the cover of shared walks; the friend as unwitting chaperone; the wedding announced as barracks gossip; the suicide committed at…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Theme: loneliness of soldiers and innocent rivalry in love — both friends love the same woman silently; the tragic irony is that neither 'wins'.  ·  Trick 2: Setting does the work: the Paris barracks vs the countryside walks — contrast the settings to explain the soldiers' longing for warmth.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. What is ironic about the ending? (2 marks) — both men's silent rivalry was unnecessary: the woman was already married.
